# Collaboration source-profile fixture

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

This keyless fixture boots the supported `dsh web --patch` source-checkout profile through Loader. Only the external model adapter is deterministic; PostgreSQL, enterprise authentication, employee publication, Workspace grants, collaboration routing, the Agent loop, and native Session streams are real. It verifies the source composition used by the private enterprise overlay, not a packaged CLI installation. Two authenticated humans and two published Bots share one room event stream with verified Schnorr signatures, distinct author keys, durable replies, and a model-driven task handoff. Channel assertions cover thread replies, reactions, search, versioned YAML, an approval gate, signed continuation, and revoked Workspace access. A signed loopback GitHub tag delivery produces a release-notes draft and a pending approval; a due scheduled workflow produces a signed service post. The webhook secret is generated in memory per run, and an invalid signature is rejected. The native Session keeps its standard work mode and immutable employee release; republishing an employee changes a new channel while an existing group retains its original release and details.

After building the Host dependencies, Client bundles, and Web frontend, run `DSH_TEST_POSTGRES_URL=postgresql://localhost/postgres pnpm exec vitest run apps/cli/tests/profiles/web/tests/collaboration-composition.integration.spec.ts`. Without that variable the test skips. The PostgreSQL role must create and drop databases and install the available `vector` extension; missing privileges fail the opted-in test.

Each run generates credentials, a unique database with a separate Session schema, a private temporary home and Workspace, and an OS-assigned loopback port. Teardown awaits WebSocket and process closure before dropping only that generated database and removing its temporary directory. Concurrent runs never share fixture state. No browser automation or external model account is required.
